trust_decision.summary: RevocationEndpoint.create_revocation_response decides, when enable_jsonp is set, to place the request-controlled 'callback' parameter (query or form body) verbatim in front of the response body as a JSONP function name, with no identifier validation, on both the error and the success path; the fix removes JSONP entirely.

landing_point.why: The summary names RevocationEndpoint and JSONP callback; the only enable_jsonp/callback use in the server code is in this one method, and the success-path wrap is the most obvious one.

fix_sites.entry_point: RevocationEndpoint.create_revocation_response (error path, e.g. GET or POST with query string; reached via pre_configured Server classes too)

fix_sites.module_kind: client-side lower-level request builder (not a sink; feature removal)
client-side lower-level request builder (not a sink; feature removal)
client wrapper (not a sink; feature removal)
client wrapper (not a sink; feature removal)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The client-side changes (oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/parameters.py:225-227, oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/clients/base.py:323) remove the feature for API consistency but are not routes into the server-side sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no second server route to dismiss. A solver could argue that only the success-path wrap (revocation.py:81-82) matters because enable_jsonp is off by default and every pre_configured Server omits it (pre_configured.py:92,145,188-190), but the error-path wrap sits six lines above in the same method.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Normal revocation responses must stay intact: error path returns JSON body e.json with Content-Type application/json, Cache-Control no-store and e.headers (WWW-Authenticate on 401); success returns ({}, '', 200). The client builder must keep appending arbitrary **kwargs to the form body.

O6_input_shapes: callback in the URL query string (Request._params is filled from uri_query, oauthlib/common.py:395); reaches the error path because GET is rejected (oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/endpoints/base.py:78-80) and POST with a query is rejected (oauthlib/oauth2/rfc6749/endpoints/base.py:85-89)
callback in the form-encoded body (oauthlib/common.py:396), reaching both the error and the success path

O7_producer.where: Request._params (oauthlib/common.py:360-396) is a generic parameter bag, not a schema or serializer specific to this protection

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An enable_jsonp option on IntrospectEndpoint that wraps e.json / the introspection JSON in request.callback, matching the revocation code.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: IntrospectEndpoint is the sibling RFC 7662 endpoint, with the same constructor shape and the same error-return idiom. A maintainer adding JSONP to revocation could plausibly have added it here too. It would be a WHERE-type sibling only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A JSONP option on the metadata endpoint's JSON response.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The metadata endpoint is a public GET JSON document, a classic JSONP target. This would also be WHERE-type only.

O9_family: XSS / content injection via unvalidated JSONP callback reflected into a script-interpretable response (CWE-79)

O10_build.toolchain: pure-Python package; pip/pytest (tox config in repo)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate or remove the callback only on the success path (revocation.py:81-82) and leave the error-path wrap (revocation.py:72-73) that GET/query requests reach.

out_of_scope_notes: With enable_jsonp=True and no callback parameter, request.callback raises AttributeError because 'callback' is not a default key in Request._params (oauthlib/common.py:360-402); this is a robustness quirk, not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell); oauthlib is a small pure-Python library and likely meets tiny_repo (<5 MB), but this was not confirmed, so the flag is not set.
Advisory text itself was not available; trust decision derived from the summary and fix diff.
present_in_latest not applicable (no O8 routes; latest release given as none).
